issue_reference: Assigned in the registration pull request rather than guessed in advance.
hypothesis: The agent's replay buffer holds 10,000 transitions and fills at around episode 37, so from that point every new transition evicts one about thirty-seven episodes old. At the 400 to 2,400 episode budgets this campaign has screened at, that ceiling is invisible: the buffer is a recent-history window either way. Over the tens of thousands of episodes the tournament agent will actually be trained for, it means the network only ever learns from roughly the last 0.1% of its own experience, which is far shorter than the horizons deep Q-learning is normally run with. This comparison varies the capacity alone over a ten-fold range - 10,000, 50,000 and 100,000 transitions - to decide the capacity the long training run is configured with. Registered before execution: a larger buffer keeps older, worse-policy transitions, so it can also hurt, and the retention and score gates are what decide which way it goes rather than the expectation stated here.

prior_evidence.settled_factors: The dose-response selected learning rate 0.0002: it beat the unchanged incumbent on score by 0.708 [0.175, 1.279] and was the only arm in that ladder to pass all three retention gates. The exploration comparison kept the random-episode period at five, its response being monotone against the hypothesis that less random play is more efficient. Both are fixed for every arm here, so capacity is the only factor that varies.
prior_evidence.budget_signal: The same configuration family gained 0.708 score over the incumbent at 400 episodes and 1.425 at 1,200, so the gain is still growing where the campaign has been stopping. That is the argument for the long run, and the argument for getting its buffer right before it starts.
prior_evidence.power: The unchanged incumbent scored 2.350, 2.200 and 1.375 on three independent forty-world sets, so no absolute score is comparable across comparisons. Every conclusion drawn here is a paired within-run contrast.

intervention.changed_factor: the replay buffer capacity, over a registered ten-fold ladder
intervention.baseline_shared_by_every_arm: the installed Task 3 incumbent as the starting point, the all_weights trainable scope, the mixed training line-up, native rewards with no approach shaping, one optimizer update per eligible transition, learning rate 0.0002 and one fully random episode in five
intervention.persistence: training-only; evaluation loads the unchanged archived agent
intervention.methodology_change: Registered under the changed setup: budget spent on depth rather than breadth, the trajectory retained at milestones because training is sequential and a peak that decays before the end should not be thrown away, and durable resume so an interrupted replica continues from minutes ago. Three replicas is deliberately thin - this comparison exists to choose a hyperparameter for the long run before tonight, not to establish a small difference between arms, and is powered and reported accordingly.
intervention.registered_risk: A wider buffer makes each checkpoint larger, because a checkpoint carries its replay. The widest arm is capped at 100,000 rather than the 200,000 first considered so that five concurrent workers stay inside the memory ceiling on this host; a ten-fold range is enough to decide the direction, and the long run can go further if the direction is favourable. The retained milestones are not evaluated by this run; the gates are decided on the final checkpoints.

random_episode_schedule: Every arm uses the registered #168 schedule at period five: for each block of five episodes, random.Random(agent_seed + 168000000 + block_index).randrange(5) selects one fully random episode and the other four are greedy.
primary_endpoint: Mean native score per game on classic-rule-based against the unchanged incumbent. Tournament placing is decided by score.

uncertainty.method: hierarchical paired bootstrap over replicas and shared worlds
uncertainty.family: one test family per arm that can be promoted; the promotion rule is conjunctive, so only the arm count is Bonferroni-adjusted
uncertainty.role: registered decision input, not a post-hoc description

selection: An arm is promotable only if every applicable integrity gate, every retention gate and every efficacy gate passes. Among promotable arms the largest mean score gain over the unchanged incumbent is chosen, and within it the median-final replica by that score. The best-looking replica is not selectable. If no arm is promotable the installed incumbent remains the submission candidate.
scientific_gates: Original cumulative Task 1/2/3 requirements are unchanged; this exploratory comparison cannot retrospectively establish any of them.
known_gate_defect: The frozen_online_weights gate is reported as not applicable, because every arm registers the scope whose purpose is to move those weights. The invalid-action gate compares each trained artifact against the unchanged reference rather than demanding a global zero it could never reach; every completed Task 4 comparison has failed it, which is a finding about fine-tuning rather than a discriminator between arms.

machine_allocation.training: 5 concurrent workers, one torch thread each
machine_allocation.latency: one worker on an otherwise idle machine; the only latency source

authorization: Owner 1BlauNitrox authorized this comparison on 16 September 2026 as the last Task 4 screen before the long training run, to decide the replay capacity that run is configured with. No automatic extension, no automatic promotion; the README and interpretation follow completed results.
